title: Budgets and stop are not enforced mid-batch on the cloud-wave path
description:
From b6e gap 4, and it is the one with teeth. The hard-stop killcheck runs BETWEEN batches, not while one is in flight: dispatchWave has no cancellation seam through its spawn-wait-collect-teardown cycle. So an operator hard stop, or a budget trip, waits for the current batch of up to max_instances containers to finish before anything reacts.

This repo has already paid for the general version of this lesson twice — cts (a budget that could not trip) and gyl (a kill switch a reboot undid) — and the same money is now spendable through a window nobody watches. Give dispatchWave a cancellation seam and check on it, rather than only at batch boundaries.

b6e also notes, correctly, that the PRE-EXISTING orchestrator path has the identical untested gap: no test asserts stop-before-first-boot or stop-between-reboot-attempts. It declined to add a timing-dependent test rather than add a flaky one, which was the right call — but the assertion is still missing on both paths, so this tick owns finding a non-racy way to make it (a synchronization seam the suite does not have anywhere yet).
